editorialPaths.title: Scaling the Impossible
editorialPaths.question: What changes when one bounded object becomes an inhabited world?
editorialPaths.description: A four-case progression through the reconstruction problem: establish a physical bill of materials, scale it into a machine, translate occupancy into structure and finally define a world-bearing habitat without losing the functional unit.

steps.note: Begin with one forged shield: a compact product system where mass, layers and primary materials can be traced directly.
Scale the same reconstruction discipline to a launch-ready vessel with a larger material architecture and an explicit construction boundary.
Turn narrative occupancy, gates and circulation into a structural shell sized for a defined first muster.
End with a world-bearing habitat whose population, service life and construction gate must remain visible in the reporting basis.

editorialPaths.title: When Time Becomes Inventory
editorialPaths.question: When does duration matter more than the object itself?
editorialPaths.description: A route through four temporal models, moving from one rebirth cycle to repeated punishment, continuous defence and century-scale maintenance. Each step changes the reference flow before it changes the answer.

steps.note: Start with one Phoenix rebirth event and see how a single cycle establishes the service boundary.
Follow the same action through 1,000 complete punishment cycles, where repetition becomes the functional unit.
Move to continuous coastal defence, where patrol frequency and operating life dominate the reconstructed system.
Finish with a century of seaworthiness and material replacement, making maintenance the identity of the object.

editorialPaths.title: Following the Gold Assumption
editorialPaths.question: How can a small precious-metal assumption control the whole result?
editorialPaths.description: Four different gold narratives expose four different accounting problems: conversion energy, primary material assignment, replication and unrecovered ceremonial use. The route follows the modelling decision, not the size of the headline result.

steps.note: Begin with a laboratory projection event where the declared conversion service makes energy the principal lens.
Assign a touch-converted goblet as primary gold equivalent and observe how the material boundary controls interpretation.
Extend the material claim across one original ring and eight equal replicas delivered over nine nights.
Close with a ceremonial rite where 50.5 kg of primary gold is explicitly assigned as unrecovered use.

editorialPaths.title: Drawing the Boundary Around Magic
editorialPaths.question: How do you model an impossible effect without inventing its mechanism?
editorialPaths.description: A guided sequence about disciplined omission. Each case defines a measurable physical service, isolates the impossible claim and keeps the cut-off visible rather than filling the gap with an invented process.

steps.note: Model one launch-ready wing pair and a minimum gliding service without supplying a fictional propulsion mechanism.
Keep the ceramic vessel physical and explicitly exclude its non-physical payload from the inventory.
Express Bifrost as one controlled activation and a ten-minute crossing window rather than an unbounded magical infrastructure.
Define success as one neutralisation and containment event, ending only when the immortal head is sealed and the pit is closed.

collections.title: Impossible Structures
collections.description: Cities, towers and labyrinths where geometry becomes inventory and construction choices determine the climate hotspot.

collections.title: Legendary Engineering
collections.description: Objects that behave like engineered systems: legendary vehicles, forged weapons, autonomous guardians and machines built to solve impossible tasks.

collections.title: Impossible Wearables
collections.description: Wearable mythical systems where leather, metal, feathers and other physical materials carry the footprint while impossible movement remains an explicitly bounded service claim.

collections.title: Systems That Never Stop
collections.description: Cases where time, repetition or continuous operation changes the answer more than the object itself.

collections.title: Mythic Threat Control
collections.description: Cases where the footprint is shaped by the system built to contain, patrol or control a mythic threat rather than by the creature alone.

collections.title: Gilded Hotspots
collections.description: Cases where a thin precious-metal surface outweighs much larger material, energy and logistics flows.

collections.title: Gold-Driven Cases
collections.description: Cases where gold intensity overwhelms much larger energy, logistics or base-material flows, making the precious-metal assumption the decisive model driver.

collections.title: Alchemy & Transmutation
collections.description: Cases where an impossible conversion into gold turns physical reconstruction, material intensity and the accounting boundary into the real analytical problem.

collections.title: Mythic Biology
collections.description: Mythic creatures translated into physical bodies and bounded services, where feed, biological emissions, regeneration and physiology proxies make the climate footprint measurable.

collections.title: Impossible Flight
collections.description: Cases where mythical flight is translated into physical bodies, wearable systems or airborne service models, making support materials, feeding and proxy choices visible even when magic itself carries no fuel burden.
